settings.description: The tonic note exercises are built around.
settings.label: Key

settings.description: The scale exercises are drawn from.
settings.label: Scale

settings.description: Choose what kind of prompt to practice: Random Notes plays an arbitrary sequence within your range; Diatonic Arpeggios plays a triad built from the selected scale.
settings.label: Test Type

settings.description: How many notes make up each test. Locked to 3 for Diatonic Arpeggios.
settings.label: Sequence Length

settings.description: How fast the test sequence plays, in beats per minute.
settings.label: Tempo (BPM)

settings.description: The instrument you're practicing on — sets its default range and note-name transposition (e.g. a B♭ instrument shows written pitches, not concert pitches).
settings.label: Instrument

settings.description: Play a short chime when a test passes or fails, in addition to the note colors.
settings.label: Play Pass/Fail Sounds

settings.description: What plays before the test sequence to establish the key: a single root note, a block chord, the chord arpeggiated, a scale run, or nothing.
settings.label: Intro Sound

settings.description: Show the expected notes on the staff before you play them, in black, turning green as you get each one right — good for learning. Off by default: the staff stays blank until you play, for a bigger challenge.
settings.label: Display Test Notes

settings.description: Show a standard key signature after the clef, so only out-of-key notes get an accidental. Off by default: every accidental is shown directly on the note.
settings.label: Use Key Signature

settings.description: How many attempts you get on a test before the app moves on.
settings.label: Max Retries

settings.description: How many extra tries you get at a single wrong note, in place, before it counts as a failed attempt and the whole test replays. Each retry used costs a few points. 0 turns this off.
settings.label: Retry Same Note

settings.description: The gap between the intro chord and the test sequence.
settings.label: Pause Before Playing

settings.description: How long a wrong note is shown before the test replays or a new one starts.
settings.label: Wrong Note Pause

settings.description: How sensitive the microphone is, on a 1 to 10 scale: higher means more sensitive (picks up quieter notes but also more background noise), lower means less sensitive. Raise it if quiet playing is missed; lower it if background noise triggers false notes.
settings.label: Mic Sensitivity

settings.description: How many consistent pitch readings in a row are needed before a note is confirmed. Higher is steadier but slower to react.
settings.label: Note Stability (frames to confirm)

settings.description: How many initial readings are discarded right after the mic starts listening, to let it settle before detection begins.
settings.label: Mic Warmup Frames

settings.description: How many shaky readings after a confirmed note are tolerated before the tracker gives up on it and starts confirming a new one.
settings.label: Grace Frames

settings.description: Snap detected pitches that are an octave off to the nearest note in your exercise's range — helps with instruments prone to octave errors.
settings.label: Octave Correction

settings.description: How strict the pitch detector is about a note being clearly periodic. Lower catches quieter or noisier notes; higher rejects more false positives.
settings.label: YIN Threshold
